title: The pool's router arm scores both parts of a split route's answer
goal: When kb_ask's router splits a question (the reader answers what the kb has, the researcher the rest), the pool record's answer, tools and checks cover both parts; today agent_bench.add keeps the second run's answer, so the reader's 'kb has:' part is not checked. Measure first how many 2026-10-08 router runs took the split route. Found by the SP-hm4qgf3t review.

gates.question: How is a split route's pool row joined from its two runs?
options: The reader's answer first, a blank line, then the researcher's; tool counts and searches summed, fetched urls concatenated
The researcher's answer alone, with the reader's checks scored on a separate row
gates.recommendation: The reader's answer first, a blank line, then the researcher's; tool counts and searches summed, fetched urls concatenated
gates.answer: The reader's answer first, a blank line, then the researcher's; tool counts and searches summed, fetched urls concatenated

notes: Blocks the next pool benchmark record: the operator asked on 2026-10-08 for the work needed before the next record to be staged as SP-2vhfsn4o. Premise run 2026-10-08 on the record's runs file: 83 of 450 router runs used both claude-haiku-4-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5 (the split route), whose reader part agent_bench.add drops (agent_bench.py:239), so their checks read the researcher's answer only. -k bench_pool passes before the work; the work adds a split-route assertion to an existing bench_pool test, which is its failing proof.
